```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import itertools
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

DOC = "PCR-005"
UO = "protein_a"
UO_TITLE = "Protein A Chromatography (Step 5)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- identity, dates
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
P = {p.key: p for p in uo.parameters}
ver, eff_date = doc_version(DOC)
scale_l = f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"
plan_appr = PLAN_APPROVAL["PCP-005"]
chron = csv("study_chronology.csv")
chron = chron[chron["step"] == UO].set_index("id")
def win(sid):
    return f"{chron.loc[sid, 'start']} to {chron.loc[sid, 'end']}"
# the characterization studies (every study but the supplementary qualification of PD-005-01)
PD = PLAN_DISCREPANCIES[DOC][0]
supp_studies = list(PD["studies"])
chron_char = chron.drop(index=supp_studies)
first_start = chron_char["start"].min()
last_end = chron_char["end"].max()
assert all(chron.loc[s, "start"] > last_end for s in supp_studies)   # the extra runs came after

def g(x):
    return f"{x:g}"
def rng(p):
    return f"{p.prange[0]:g}–{p.prange[1]:g}"
def nor(p):
    return f"{p.nor[0]:g}–{p.nor[1]:g}"
def yn(b):
    return "Yes" if b else "No"
def f0(x):
    return f"{x:,.0f}"
def f2(x):
    return f"{x:.2f}"
def f3(x):
    return f"{x:.3f}"
def p3(p):
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"
def pf(p):
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"
def andjoin(xs):
    xs = list(xs)
    return xs[0] if len(xs) == 1 else ", ".join(xs[:-1]) + " and " + xs[-1]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- design structure
n_scr = doe_runs(UO, "screening"); n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
cp_scr = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"); cp_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
n_fact = n_scr - cp_scr
n_axial = n_rsm - n_fact - cp_rsm
n_fac = len(D.rsm_factors(UO))
# the design centre is the set-point for every design factor, so set-point and design-centre
# analyses coincide at this step
assert all(abs(D.to_coded(UO, q, P[q].setpoint)) < 1e-9 for q in D.rsm_factors(UO))
rp = report_params(UO)
n_par = len(rp)
n_multi = int((rp["Study"] == "multivariate").sum()); n_uni = n_par - n_multi
cls = rp["Class"].value_counts()
n_wc = int(cls.get("WC-CPP", 0)); n_cpp = int(cls.get("CPP", 0)); n_kpp = int(cls.get("KPP", 0)); n_gpp = int(cls.get("GPP", 0))
rt_set = P["bed_height"].setpoint / P["flow"].setpoint * 60
rt_hi = P["bed_height"].setpoint / P["flow"].prange[1] * 60
rt_lo = P["bed_height"].setpoint / P["flow"].prange[0] * 60
rt_short = P["bed_height"].prange[0] / P["flow"].setpoint * 60
mc_n = f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- criteria
iac = D.iac_table(UO).set_index("response")
acc = {r: D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) for r in ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "leached_protein_a_ppm", "lmw_cesds_pct"]}
crit_hcp = f0(acc["pool_hcp_ng_mg"][1]); crit_lpa = f0(acc["leached_protein_a_ppm"][1]); crit_frag = f2(acc["lmw_cesds_pct"][1])
ds_hcp = g(iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "ds_high"]); ds_lpa = g(iac.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "ds_high"]); ds_frag = f2(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "ds_high"])
fold_hcp = f0(iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "downstream_fold"]); fold_lpa = g(iac.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "downstream_fold"])
fold_frag = f2(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "downstream_fold"]); add_frag = g(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "downstream_added"])
apri_hcp = f0(iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "iac_high_apriori"]); apri_frag = f2(iac.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "iac_high_apriori"])
basis_hcp = D.acceptance_basis(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"); basis_lpa = D.acceptance_basis(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm")
basis_frag = D.acceptance_basis(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct")
widened = {r: bool(iac.loc[r, "widened"]) for r in iac.index}
tightened = {r: bool(iac.loc[r, "tightened"]) for r in iac.index}
assert widened["pool_hcp_ng_mg"] and not widened["lmw_cesds_pct"] and not widened["leached_protein_a_ppm"]
assert not any(tightened.values())
assert "widened" in basis_hcp and "widened" not in basis_frag
r1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO).set_index("response")
r1_hcp = f0(r1.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "high"]); r1_margin = g(r1.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "margin"])
assert acc["pool_hcp_ng_mg"][1] > r1.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "high"]       # wider than Version 1.0
agg_lim = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw"); acid_lim = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants")
agg_crit = f2(agg_lim[1]); acid_crit = f"{acid_lim[0]:g}–{acid_lim[1]:g}"
lof_alpha = THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"]; max_gap = THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"]

# the downstream values these criteria rely on, and the verification that widened two of them
ver_all = D.iac_verification()
rel = ver_all[(ver_all["cqa"].isin(["hcp", "leached_protein_a", "fragments_lmw"])) & (ver_all["step_key"] != UO)]
rel_chk = rel[rel["met"].notna()]
n_rel = len(rel); n_rel_chk = len(rel_chk); n_rel_conf = int(rel_chk["met"].astype(bool).sum())
rel_all_conf = bool(n_rel_conf == n_rel_chk)
rel_unchk_lpa = bool((rel[rel["met"].isna()]["cqa"] == "leached_protein_a").all())
VR = {(r["step_key"], r["cqa"]): r for _, r in rel.iterrows()}
v_cex_hcp = VR[("cex", "hcp")]; v_aex_hcp = VR[("aex", "hcp")]; v_cex_frag = VR[("cex", "fragments_lmw")]
v_vi_frag = VR[("viral_inactivation", "fragments_lmw")]
# cation exchange host cell protein: bound better than the platform, adequate model, so it widened
assert bool(v_cex_hcp["widening_supported"]) and bool(v_cex_hcp["model_adequate"])
assert v_cex_hcp["r2_minus_pred_r2"] <= max_gap and v_cex_hcp["p_lack_of_fit"] >= lof_alpha
assert v_cex_hcp["predicted_nor_bound95"] > v_cex_hcp["assumed"] > v_cex_hcp["observed_edge"]
# anion exchange host cell protein and cation exchange fragments: bound better, model not adequate
for v in (v_aex_hcp, v_cex_frag):
    assert v["predicted_nor_bound95"] > v["assumed"] and not bool(v["model_adequate"]) and not bool(v["widening_supported"])
    assert v["r2_minus_pred_r2"] > max_gap and v["p_lack_of_fit"] >= lof_alpha
assert bool(v_aex_hcp["met"]) and bool(v_cex_frag["met"]) and bool(v_vi_frag["met"])
# low-pH inactivation fragments: the bound is better than the platform increase, the model is not adequate
assert not bool(v_vi_frag["widening_supported"]) and not bool(v_vi_frag["model_adequate"])
assert v_vi_frag["predicted_nor_bound95"] < v_vi_frag["assumed"] and v_vi_frag["r2_minus_pred_r2"] > max_gap
fold_ratio_check = v_cex_hcp["predicted_nor_bound95"] * v_aex_hcp["assumed"]
assert abs(fold_ratio_check - iac.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "downstream_fold"]) / fold_ratio_check < 1e-3
n_rsm_cex = doe_runs("cex", "rsm"); n_rsm_aex = doe_runs("aex", "rsm")
cp_rsm_cex = doe_centre_points("cex", "rsm"); cp_rsm_aex = doe_centre_points("aex", "rsm")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scale-down model offsets
OFF = T.sdm_offsets_data([UO]).set_index("output")                       # all set-point runs
OFF0 = T.sdm_offsets_data([UO], studies=["S-PA-SDM"]).set_index("output")  # the planned runs alone
sdm_all_q = bool(OFF["qualified"].all()); sdm0_all_q = bool(OFF0["qualified"].all())
assert sdm_all_q and not sdm0_all_q
assert not OFF0.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "qualified"] and OFF0.loc["leached_protein_a_ppm", "qualified"]
assert not OFF0.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "met_lo"]           # planned runs: fails at the low end
# the protein load NOR: as characterized, and as narrowed by this report (Version 2.0)
LOAD = P["load"]
load_nor_char = f"{LOAD.nor_characterized[0]:g}–{LOAD.nor_characterized[1]:g}"
load_nor_new = f"{LOAD.nor[0]:g}–{LOAD.nor[1]:g}"
assert LOAD.nor[0] == LOAD.nor_characterized[0] and LOAD.nor[1] < LOAD.nor_characterized[1]
assert all(p.nor == p.nor_characterized for p in uo.parameters if p.key != "load")
with D.characterized_nor():
    q_char = D.offset_qualification(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
    q_char_lpa = D.offset_qualification(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm")
    with D.offset_at("lo"):
        pl_char_lo = D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
    pt_char = D.par_table(UO)
    nor_met_char_point = D.nor_met(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
assert not q_char["qualified"] and not q_char["met_lo"] and q_char["met_point"] and q_char["met_hi"]
assert q_char_lpa["qualified"]
with D.offset_at("lo"):
    pl_new_lo = D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
with D.offset_at("lo", ["S-PA-SDM"]):
    pl_plan_lo = D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
pl_new_point = D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
assert pl_char_lo > acc["pool_hcp_ng_mg"][1] >= pl_new_lo and pl_plan_lo > acc["pool_hcp_ng_mg"][1]
par_same_char = bool((pt_char["PAR (NOR)"].values == D.par_table(UO)["PAR (NOR)"].values).all())
judged_out = [o for o in OFF.index if OFF.loc[o, "judged"]]
assert judged_out == ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "leached_protein_a_ppm"]
n_sd_all = int(OFF.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "n_sd"]); n_m = int(OFF.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "n_m"])
n_sd_plan = int(OFF0.loc["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "n_sd"]); n_sd_supp = n_sd_all - n_sd_plan
assert n_sd_supp == CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"]["supplementary"][UO]["n"]
off_ci = f"{100 * D.sdm_offset(UO, 'pool_hcp_ng_mg')['ci']:.0f}"
off_df = D.sdm_offset(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")["df"]
off_hcp = D.sdm_offset(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"); off_hcp0 = D.sdm_offset(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", ["S-PA-SDM"])
off_lpa = D.sdm_offset(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm"); off_lpa0 = D.sdm_offset(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm", ["S-PA-SDM"])
d_hcp = off_hcp["offset"]; d_lpa = off_lpa["offset"]
narrow_pct = 100 * (1 - off_hcp["half"] / off_hcp0["half"])
lpa_below = bool(off_lpa["hi"] < 0)                       # whole interval below zero
assert lpa_below and bool(off_lpa0["hi"] < 0)
hcp_ci_zero = bool(off_hcp["lo"] < 0 < off_hcp["hi"])
_sdm = csv("sdm_qualification.csv"); _sdm = _sdm[_sdm["step"] == UO]
lpa_sd_runs = _sdm.loc[_sdm["scale"] == "scale-down", "leached_protein_a_ppm"]
lpa_each_below = bool((lpa_sd_runs < off_lpa["mean_m"]).all())
# the criterion as the scale-down result is judged: the criterion plus the offset
judge_hcp = acc["pool_hcp_ng_mg"][1] + d_hcp
def ok(resp, y):
    return np.asarray(D.meets_acceptance(UO, resp, y), dtype=bool)
# conclusions are the same at both ends of the interval (Yes / Yes / Yes for both judged outputs)
for o in judged_out:
    assert OFF.loc[o, "met_lo"] and OFF.loc[o, "met_point"] and OFF.loc[o, "met_hi"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model fits and adequacy
RESP = ["pool_hcp_ng_mg", "step_yield", "leached_protein_a_ppm", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
F = {r: D.fit(UO, "rsm", r) for r in RESP}
def gap(r):
    return F[r]["R2"] - F[r]["predR2"]
ADEQ = {r: dict(sig=F[r]["p"] < lof_alpha, lof=F[r]["p_lof"] >= lof_alpha, pred=gap(r) <= max_gap) for r in RESP}
for r in RESP:
    ADEQ[r]["all"] = all(ADEQ[r].values())
assert ADEQ["pool_hcp_ng_mg"]["all"] and not ADEQ["step_yield"]["pred"]
assert not ADEQ["leached_protein_a_ppm"]["sig"] and not ADEQ["lmw_cesds_pct"]["sig"]

# reduced step-yield model: the terms significant in both designs, kept hierarchical
dY = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
red_terms = ["coded_load", "coded_flow", "coded_end_collect", "coded_load:coded_flow"]
mY = smf.ols("step_yield ~ " + " + ".join(red_terms), dY).fit()
hY = mY.get_influence().hat_matrix_diag
predY = 1 - np.sum((mY.resid / (1 - hY)) ** 2) / np.sum((dY["step_yield"] - dY["step_yield"].mean()) ** 2)
sseY = float(np.sum(mY.resid ** 2)); df_peY = F["step_yield"]["df_pe"]; ss_peY = F["step_yield"]["ss_pe"]
df_lofY = int(mY.df_resid) - df_peY
FlofY = ((sseY - ss_peY) / df_lofY) / (ss_peY / df_peY)
p_lofY = float(sstat.f.sf(FlofY, df_lofY, df_peY))
RED = dict(R2=mY.rsquared, adj=mY.rsquared_adj, pred=predY, p=mY.f_pvalue, p_lof=p_lofY, gap=mY.rsquared - predY,
           k=len(red_terms) + 1)
RED["all"] = bool(RED["p"] < lof_alpha and RED["p_lof"] >= lof_alpha and RED["gap"] <= max_gap)
assert RED["all"]
same_verdict_adj = all(((F[r]["adjR2"] - F[r]["predR2"]) <= max_gap) == ADEQ[r]["pred"] for r in RESP) and \
    ((RED["adj"] - RED["pred"]) <= max_gap) == (RED["gap"] <= max_gap)

adeq_rows = []
for r in RESP:
    f = F[r]
    adeq_rows.append([D.RESP_LABEL[r], "full quadratic", f3(f["R2"]), f3(f["adjR2"]), f3(f["predR2"]), f3(gap(r)),
                      p3(f["p"]), p3(f["p_lof"]), yn(ADEQ[r]["all"])])
adeq_rows.insert(2, [D.RESP_LABEL["step_yield"], f"reduced ({len(red_terms)} terms)", f3(RED["R2"]), f3(RED["adj"]), f3(RED["pred"]), f3(RED["gap"]),
                     p3(RED["p"]), p3(RED["p_lof"]), yn(RED["all"])])
adeq_df = pd.DataFrame(adeq_rows, columns=["Response", "Model", "R²", "Adj. R²", "Pred. R²", "R² − pred. R²",
                                           "Model p", "Lack of fit p", "Criteria 2–4 met"])

# residual checks (criterion 5): |residual| on predicted, and Cook's distance against 4/n
cook_lim = 4 / n_rsm
res_rows, RES = [], {}
for r in RESP:
    m = F[r]["model"]
    cd = m.get_influence().cooks_distance[0]
    gm = sm.OLS(np.abs(m.resid.values), sm.add_constant(m.fittedvalues.values)).fit()
    go = sm.OLS(m.resid.values, sm.add_constant(F[r]["df"]["run_order"].values.astype(float))).fit()
    RES[r] = dict(p_slope=gm.pvalues[1], p_order=go.pvalues[1], cmax=cd.max(), crun=int(F[r]["df"]["run"].values[cd.argmax()]),
                  n_over=int((cd > cook_lim).sum()), cd=cd)
    res_rows.append([D.RESP_LABEL[r], p3(gm.pvalues[1]), p3(go.pvalues[1]), f2(cd.max()), str(RES[r]["crun"]), str(RES[r]["n_over"])])
res_df = pd.DataFrame(res_rows, columns=["Response", "p, absolute residual\non predicted", "p, residual\non run order",
                                         "Largest Cook's\ndistance", "Run", "Runs\nabove 4/n"])
slope_ok = all(RES[r]["p_slope"] >= lof_alpha for r in RESP)
order_ok = all(RES[r]["p_order"] >= lof_alpha for r in RESP)
assert slope_ok and order_ok
p_order_min = min(RES[r]["p_order"] for r in RESP)
n_over_min = min(RES[r]["n_over"] for r in RESP); n_over_max = max(RES[r]["n_over"] for r in RESP)
assert n_over_min > 0                                     # criterion 5 fails for every model
mean_lev = (F["pool_hcp_ng_mg"]["model"].df_model + 1) / n_rsm

# influence of single runs on the pool HCP conclusion (deletion of each run above 4/n)
fH = F["pool_hcp_ng_mg"]; XH = fH["model"].model.exog; yH = fH["df"]["pool_hcp_ng_mg"].values
nor_grid = list(itertools.product(*[[D.to_coded(UO, q, P[q].nor[0]), 0.0, D.to_coded(UO, q, P[q].nor[1])] for q in fH["factors"]]))
Gc = pd.DataFrame(nor_grid, columns=["coded_" + q for q in fH["factors"]])
XG = D._design(Gc, fH["factors"], True)[0].values
loo_max, loo_dA, loo_dB = [], [], []
pA, pB = fH["model"].params.iloc[1], fH["model"].params.iloc[2]
for i in np.where(RES["pool_hcp_ng_mg"]["cd"] > cook_lim)[0]:
    mi = sm.OLS(np.delete(yH, i), np.delete(XH, i, axis=0)).fit()
    # judged as the PAR analysis judges: the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run over the NOR
    loo_max.append(float(mi.get_prediction(XG).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)["obs_ci_upper"].max()))
    loo_dA.append(abs(mi.params[1] / pA - 1)); loo_dB.append(abs(mi.params[2] / pB - 1))
loo_lo, loo_hi = min(loo_max) - d_hcp, max(loo_max) - d_hcp      # at manufacturing scale
loo_dmax = 100 * max(max(loo_dA), max(loo_dB))
loo_ok = bool(ok("pool_hcp_ng_mg", [max(loo_max)])[0])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- centre points
cv_s = D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
cv_r = D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm").set_index("Response")
L = D.RESP_LABEL

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- effects and coefficients
def se_row(resp, term):
    e = D.screening_effects_df(UO, resp).set_index("Term")
    return e.loc[term]
def co_row(resp, term):
    c = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, resp).set_index("Term")
    return c.loc[term]
scr_fit = D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
eH = {t: se_row("pool_hcp_ng_mg", t) for t in ["A", "B", "AB", "C", "D"]}
eY = {t: se_row("step_yield", t) for t in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "AC", "CD", "BD"]}
cH = {t: co_row("pool_hcp_ng_mg", t) for t in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "AB", "AC", "AD", "BD", "B²"]}
cL = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm")
cL_sig = cL[(cL["p-value"] < 0.05) & (cL["Term"] != "Intercept")]["Term"].tolist()
cF = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "lmw_cesds_pct").set_index("Term")
slope_hi = cH["B"]["Coef."] + cH["AB"]["Coef."]   # pH coefficient at high load (A = +1)
slope_lo = cH["B"]["Coef."] - cH["AB"]["Coef."]   # at low load (A = -1)
yred = mY.params
yC_hi = yred["coded_flow"] + yred["coded_load:coded_flow"]
yC_lo = yred["coded_flow"] - yred["coded_load:coded_flow"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- descriptive (no adequate model)
dS = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
lpa_all = pd.concat([dS["leached_protein_a_ppm"], dY["leached_protein_a_ppm"]])
lpa_min, lpa_max = lpa_all.min(), lpa_all.max()
lpa_max_m = lpa_max - d_lpa                                   # at manufacturing scale
lpa_ok = bool(ok("leached_protein_a_ppm", lpa_all.values).all())
fr = dY["lmw_cesds_pct"].dropna()
fr_n, fr_min, fr_max = len(fr), fr.min(), fr.max()
fr_ok = bool(ok("lmw_cesds_pct", fr.values).all())
sec_minus = (dY["lmw_sec_pct"] - dY["lmw_cesds_pct"]).dropna()
hcp_all_max = dY["pool_hcp_ng_mg"].max(); hcp_all_min = dY["pool_hcp_ng_mg"].min()
y_min, y_max = 100 * dY["step_yield"].min(), 100 * dY["step_yield"].max()
_both = pd.concat([dS, dY])
_ov = _both[~ok("pool_hcp_ng_mg", _both["pool_hcp_ng_mg"].values)]
n_hcp_over = len(_ov)
hcp_over_corner = bool(n_hcp_over > 0 and (_ov["load"] == P["load"].prange[1]).all() and (_ov["elution_ph"] == P["elution_ph"].prange[0]).all())

HOLD_ATTR = [("hmw_pct", "Aggregate, HMW (%)", "bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw", agg_lim[1], 2),

HOLD, hold_rows = {}, []
for col, lab, key, resp, crit, nd in HOLD_ATTR:
    # fragments: no adequate model (Results), so the highest measured result of the retained
    # response-surface pools, which span the NOR and the range studied beyond it
    lim = D.nor_prediction_limit(key, resp, side="upper") if key != UO else float(fr_max)

        hold_rows.append([lab, tmp, f"{lim:.{nd}f}", f"{inc:.{nd}f}", f"{lim + inc:.{nd}f}", f"≤ {crit:.{nd}f}",

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tables as a report sets them
def showt(df):
    """A pre-formatted frame as a pipe table, without re-parsing its numbers."""
    print(df.to_markdown(index=False, disable_numparse=True))
def tidy(df, scale=None, scale_rows=None):
    """Format a statistics frame: no scientific notation, p-values fixed, step yield in %.
    ``scale`` multiplies the named columns (all rows, or only rows whose first cell is in scale_rows)."""
    d = df.copy().reset_index(drop=True)
    first = d.columns[0]
    for c in d.columns:
        if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(d[c]) or pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(d[c]):
            continue
        def f(v, i, c=c):
            if pd.isna(v):
                return ""
            if scale and c in scale and (scale_rows is None or d.loc[i, first] in scale_rows):
                v = v * 100
            if c in ("p-value", "Model p", "Lack of fit p"):
                return p3(v)
            if c in ("R²", "Adj. R²", "Pred. R²"):
                return f3(v)
            if c in ("t", "F"):
                return f"{v:.2f}"
            if c in ("N", "n", "df"):
                return f"{int(v)}"
            if c == "%CV":
                return f"{v:.2f}"
            return T.num(v)
        d[c] = [f(v, i) for i, v in enumerate(d[c])]
    return d

assert cF.loc["B", "p-value"] < 0.05 and cF.loc["B", "Coef."] < 0
assert hdr[(t_warm, "hmw_pct")] > hdr[(t_cold, "hmw_pct")] and hdr[(t_warm, "acidic_pct")] > hdr[(t_cold, "acidic_pct")]
assert hdr[(t_cold, "lmw_cesds_pct")] > 0 and hdr[(t_warm, "lmw_cesds_pct")] > 0
# the region the model excludes at set-point flow and pool collection: high load, low pH only
_y0 = D.predict(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", coded={"load": _A.ravel(), "elution_ph": _B.ravel()})
_bad = ~ok("pool_hcp_ng_mg", _y0)
assert _bad.any() and (_A.ravel()[_bad] > 0).all() and (_B.ravel()[_bad] < 0).all()
# wholly below the elution buffer pH NOR; how far down in protein load it reaches
assert (_B.ravel()[_bad] < D.to_coded(UO, "elution_ph", P["elution_ph"].nor[0])).all()
ds_load_min = float(D.to_natural(UO, "load", _A.ravel()[_bad].min()))
ds_ph_max = float(D.to_natural(UO, "elution_ph", _B.ravel()[_bad].max()))
ds_in_load_nor = bool(ds_load_min <= P["load"].nor[1])
assert corner_fail
assert ok("pool_hcp_ng_mg", [nor_corner_m + d_hcp])[0]
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report presents the process characterization of the Protein A chromatography step (Step 5) of the A-Mab drug substance process. Protein A chromatography is the capture step of the purification train. It removes most of the host cell protein and DNA of the clarified harvest, and it adds one impurity of its own, Protein A ligand that leaches from the resin. The characterization studies were run under the approved plan PCP-005 in a scale-down model of the commercial column, between `{python} first_start` and `{python} last_end`. Supplementary set-point runs of the scale-down model followed from `{python} win('S-PA-SDM2')`. The report follows the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011], the enhanced approach of ICH Q8 and ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11] and the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. This is Version `{python} ver` of the report. It re-analyses the experiments of Version 1.0 against the criteria of PCMP-001 Version 2.0, issued under the investigation INV-001 into acceptance criteria set after the data were seen, and it adds the fragment results by nrCE-SDS.

The step has `{python} n_par` process parameters. Of these, `{python} n_multi` were studied in a `{python} n_scr`-run screening design followed by a `{python} n_rsm`-run response-surface design, and `{python} n_uni` were studied one factor at a time. Protein load and elution buffer pH were classified as WC-CPPs, load flow rate and end of pool collect as KPPs, and operating temperature and bed height as GPPs. No parameter of the step was classified as a CPP.

- F1. Over all `{python} n_sd_all` scale-down set-point runs, the offset of the scale-down model from manufacturing scale is `{python} f0(d_hcp)` ng/mg for pool host cell protein and `{python} f2(d_lpa)` ppm for leached Protein A. Leached Protein A is lower in the scale-down model, for an expected cause given in @sec-sdm. The model is qualified for leached Protein A over the NOR as characterized.
- F2. At the protein load NOR as characterized, `{python} load_nor_char` g/L resin, the scale-down model is not qualified for pool host cell protein. With the offset at the low end of its `{python} off_ci` % confidence interval, the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run over the NOR reaches `{python} f0(pl_char_lo)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, above the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. This report therefore narrows the protein load NOR to `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin. At the narrowed NOR the same limit is `{python} f0(pl_new_lo)` ng/mg, and the model is qualified for pool host cell protein at both ends of the interval (@sec-sdm). On the `{python} n_sd_plan` set-point runs that PCP-005 planned, the model would not be qualified for pool host cell protein even at the narrowed NOR (@sec-dev).
- F3. Pool host cell protein rises with protein load and as elution buffer pH falls, and the two parameters interact. It falls as the end of pool collect is extended. The response-surface model for pool host cell protein is significant, shows no lack of fit and predicts left-out runs within the limit of PCP-005 §7 (criteria 2 to 4). It does not meet the limit on influential runs, a Cook's distance below 4/n (criterion 5, finding F8, @sec-rsm).
- F4. Step yield rises with end of pool collect and falls with protein load and load flow rate, and flow rate costs yield mainly at high load. The full quadratic model for step yield fails the limit on predictive power. A reduced model with the terms significant in both designs meets the tests of significance, lack of fit and predictive power. Like every model of the study, it does not meet the limit on influential runs (@sec-rsm).
- F5. No adequate model results for leached Protein A, so its dependence on the parameters of the multivariate design is not resolved. Every run of both designs `{python} 'met' if lpa_ok else 'did not meet'` the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm at manufacturing scale, with a highest result of `{python} f2(lpa_max_m)` ppm (@sec-rsm).
- F6. Fragments by nrCE-SDS fall slightly as elution buffer pH rises, and no adequate model results, so the decision rests on the measured results. All `{python} fr_n` response-surface pools `{python} 'met' if fr_ok else 'did not meet'` the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %, with a highest result of `{python} f2(fr_max)` % (@sec-rsm).
- F7. Every output `{python} 'met' if all_nor_met else 'did not meet'` its criterion across the NOR in force at manufacturing scale. For pool host cell protein the NOR-propagated PAR of elution buffer pH is `{python} hcp_par_nor['elution_ph']`, narrower than its range studied of `{python} rng(P['elution_ph'])`. The PAR of every other parameter, and every PAR for leached Protein A and fragments, spans the range studied. Pool host cell protein exceeds its criterion only in the corner of high protein load and low elution buffer pH, below the NOR of elution buffer pH (@sec-ds, @sec-par).
- F8. No residual trend against the predicted value or the run order was found for any response. Between `{python} n_over_min` and `{python} n_over_max` runs of each response-surface model exceed a Cook's distance of 4/n, so the limit on influential runs of PCP-005 §7 (criterion 5) is not met. With any one of these runs deleted, the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run over the NOR stays `{python} 'below' if loo_ok else 'above'` the criterion for pool host cell protein (@sec-resid).
- F9. Held at elution pH for `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm`, the Protein A eluate `{python} 'met' if h_ok else 'did not meet'` the hold rule of PCP-005. That rule adds the largest increase over the hold to the highest level expected in the pool, and requires the sum to stay within the criterion. The lowest level of acidic variants expected in the pool is below the floor of `{python} g(acid_lim[0])` % before any hold, a result of the production bioreactor (PCR-003). Aggregate and acidic variants rose more at `{python} t_warm`. Fragments by nrCE-SDS rose at both temperatures, and the data do not show a temperature dependence (@sec-hold).
- F10. No difference from the set-point runs was detected at either end of the ranges of operating temperature and bed height, and every result `{python} 'met' if uni_ok else 'did not meet'` its criterion. With `{python} uni_reps` runs at each end the intervals are wide (@sec-uni).
- F11. The effect of end of pool collect on pool host cell protein, and its interactions with protein load and elution buffer pH, have opposite signs in the screening and the response-surface designs. The difference is larger than the noise of the screening design, and its cause was not identified (@sec-rsm).

The proven acceptable ranges and the design space rest on the response-surface model for pool host cell protein and on a scale-down model qualified for that output at the narrowed protein load NOR. The KPP classes of load flow rate and end of pool collect rest on the reduced model for step yield and on the direction of the yield effects, which both designs show (@sec-class). The main effects of protein load and elution buffer pH agree in direction with the A-Mab case study. Load flow rate has no significant effect on pool host cell protein (@sec-mech).

At commercial scale the integrated model of the train gives a Cpk of `{python} f2(cpk_hcp)` for host cell protein and `{python} f2(cpk_frag)` for fragments in the drug substance. `{python} 'Both are above' if cpk_met else 'Not both are above'` the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` that PCMP-001 sets. The Cpk for leached Protein A is `{python} f2(cpk_lpa)`, and `{python} 'no simulated batch' if n_oos == 0 else str(n_oos) + ' simulated batches'` of `{python} mc_n` fell outside these criteria. The Cpk for leached Protein A is not meaningful, because the simulated drug substance values lie below the limit of quantitation of the ELISA. The register lists `{python} n_dev` deviations for the studies of the step, an elution buffer prepared below its target pH (DEV-005-01) and an out-of-trend leached Protein A result that was re-assayed (DEV-005-02). Both were investigated and the affected data were retained.
 The report also records `{python} n_pd` discrepancies from the plan. PD-005-01 covers the supplementary set-point runs of the scale-down model qualification, and PD-005-02 the influence analysis on which the conclusion for pool host cell protein rests. The results roll up into the Process Characterization Master Report PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose primary mechanism of action is antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity. It is developed by `{python} COMPANY` and is being transferred from development at the sending site to commercial drug substance manufacture at `{python} scale_l` L scale at the receiving site, under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. The drug substance is purified by the platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small virus retentive filtration and UF/DF.

Protein A chromatography is the first chromatographic step of the purification train. It is operated in bind and elute mode. The resin binds the antibody from the clarified harvest at neutral pH, while host cell protein, DNA and most other components of the feed are removed in the load flow-through and the wash. A low-pH buffer elutes the antibody into a small volume, and the eluate passes to low-pH viral inactivation (Step 6) without neutralization. The step is the principal point of clearance for host cell protein and DNA, and it partly clears fragments. It introduces one attribute of the CQA register, leached Protein A. Although Protein A chromatography removes some virus, no viral clearance claim is made for this step [@amab2009]. The viral clearance claim of the process rests on low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration, and it is consolidated in PCMR-001.

## Objectives

The objectives of the characterization were the following, as PCP-005 §2 states them.

1. To estimate the offset between the scale-down model and manufacturing scale for each output of the step, and to qualify the model by that offset for each output with a criterion.
2. To identify which of the `{python} n_multi` parameters of the multivariate design, and which of their two-factor interactions, affect pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A.
3. To fit response-surface models for pool host cell protein, step yield, leached Protein A and fragments by nrCE-SDS, and to judge their adequacy for prediction.
4. To determine the PAR of each multivariate parameter for each attribute with a criterion at the step.
5. To establish the effect of operating temperature and bed height over their ranges, one factor at a time.
6. To establish how long, and at which temperature, the Protein A eluate may be held at elution pH before viral inactivation.
7. To provide the data for the classification of every parameter of the step under SOP-4001, and to support the Stage 2 ranges and the control strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is part of Stage 1 (process design) of the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) and ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11], in which prior knowledge and risk assessment identify the parameters that may affect quality, and designed experiments then measure and bound those effects. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as ICH Q8(R2) describes it, and risk is managed under ICH Q9 [@ichq9]. The classification of parameters follows the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009], as PCMP-001 §7.7 applies it. The documents this report depends on and feeds are listed below.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The same capture step has been used to purify the platform antibodies X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and A-Mab through clinical manufacture [@amab2009]. Staphylococcal Protein A, immobilized on the resin, binds the Fc region of the antibody at the interface between the second and third constant domains of the heavy chain. When the pH is lowered, histidine residues at this interface become protonated, the interaction weakens, and the antibody is released.

Host cell protein reaches the eluate by two routes. Some binds to the resin backbone or to the ligand. Some associates with the antibody through electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, which the wash does not disrupt while the antibody stays bound to the ligand. A lower elution pH protonates more histidine and acidic residues, which disrupts more of both kinds of association and releases more host cell protein with the product. Pool host cell protein was therefore expected to rise as elution buffer pH falls. In the A-Mab case study pool host cell protein also rose with protein load [@amab2009], and the same direction was expected here. Pool host cell protein is reported per mass of antibody, and host cell protein that travels with the antibody rises in proportion to it. That route alone does not explain a rise with load, and no mechanism for the rise with load was assumed. Both parameters act on the host cell protein that is eluted, so an interaction between them was possible, and the designs can estimate it.

Step yield is lost when antibody breaks through during the load or remains on the column at the end of collection. Binding is limited by diffusion into the pores of the bead. For this reason breakthrough rises as the load approaches the dynamic binding capacity and as the residence time falls. A higher load flow rate shortens the residence time and lowers the dynamic binding capacity, and this costs yield only when the bed is close to capacity. Yield was therefore expected to fall with flow rate mainly at high load, and to rise as the end of pool collect is extended into the tail of the elution peak.

Leached Protein A comes from hydrolysis of the coupling chemistry and from cleavage of exposed ligand by proteases that the clarified harvest carries into the column. The leached fragments elute with the antibody because they still bind Fc. Leaching is highest on new resin, in its first cycles. Neither the life of the resin nor the protease activity of the load is a setting of the run, so within the ranges of one run leached Protein A was expected to be flat.


A fragment is captured only if it still carries Fc. Fab fragments flow through with the load, and the pool carries less fragment than the feed. A lower elution pH may add a little acid-catalysed hinge hydrolysis during elution. The pool also still carries host cell protein, part of which elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC and is read as fragment. SEC therefore overstates fragments in this matrix, and nrCE-SDS does not (INV-001 finding 6). DNA is polyanionic and does not bind Protein A. Its clearance is large and was not expected to depend on the operating parameters within their ranges.

Protein A, when operated under platform conditions, does not separate glycan variants or charge variants, because it binds the Fc region independently of both [@amab2009]. Nor does it separate aggregate from monomer, since both carry Fc. In the Protein A characterization of the case study no process parameter had a significant effect on aggregate [@amab2009]. Aggregate formation at low pH over the inactivation hold is characterized in PCR-006. For these reasons glycan variants, charge variants and aggregate were not responses of the designs.

## Quality attributes in scope

Leached Protein A is the only attribute of the CQA register that this step introduces. The step is also the principal point of clearance for host cell protein and DNA, and it partly clears fragments. @tbl-cqa lists the attributes in scope with their drug substance criteria and the criticality level the register assigns. The register treats criticality as a continuum, as the A-Mab case study does [@amab2009]. Each attribute is a CQA with a level from very low (VL) to very high (VH), assigned with Tool #1, whose score is the product of impact and uncertainty.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["leached_protein_a", "hcp", "fragments_lmw", "residual_dna", "aggregates_hmw"]))
print()
print(": Quality attributes in scope of this report, with the drug substance criterion and criticality. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

The drug substance criteria do not apply to the Protein A pool directly. Cation exchange and anion exchange remove host cell protein, leached Protein A and fragments after this step, and judging the pool against the drug substance limit would fail every acceptable run. Each output of the step with a downstream dependence is therefore judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion (@sec-par). Residual DNA and aggregate were measured for information. Step yield is a performance attribute without an acceptance criterion, and it is used for the classification of parameters that act on process performance.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 assessed every parameter of the step before characterization began. Each parameter was ranked on its potential impact on the CQAs and on process performance, and on its potential to interact with other parameters. RA-001 gives the scores and the rationale.

Protein load, elution buffer pH, load flow rate and end of pool collect were assigned to multivariate study. Each carries an effect expected from the mechanism, and the interactions of protein load with elution buffer pH and with load flow rate can only be estimated in a design that varies the parameters together. Operating temperature and bed height were assigned to univariate study. A higher temperature speeds the diffusion of the antibody into the pores, which raises the dynamic binding capacity, and it strengthens the hydrophobic contacts at the Fc–ligand interface, which makes elution slightly less complete. Over the range studied both effects were expected to be small against those of load and pH, and the resin manufacturer specifies binding capacity across that range. Bed height is held by the packing specification in manufacture, and at constant linear velocity it sets the residence time.

The ranges studied are between `{python} f'{wr_min:.1f}'` and `{python} f'{wr_max:.1f}'` times the width of the NOR. They show how the step behaves near and beyond the edges of routine operation, and they bound the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The scale-down model is a laboratory column packed with the commercial Protein A resin and operated under SOP-2007 on the scaling principles of PCMP-001 §5. The bed height and the residence time of the commercial column were kept. Load, wash and elution volumes were normalized to column volumes, and buffers were made to the commercial recipes. Column efficiency was checked by plate count and peak asymmetry after packing. PCP-005 sets no criterion for either, and both are reported for information.

The model was qualified under SOP-1001 by the offset rule of PCMP-001 §7.1, as PCP-005 §5.1 applies it. Set-point runs of the scale-down model were compared with `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches of A-Mab run at set-point. The outputs compared were pool host cell protein, leached Protein A, step yield, and column efficiency as plates per metre and peak asymmetry. The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches. It is reported with its two-sided `{python} off_ci` % confidence interval, from a Student t interval with pooled variance. Every judgement of a scale-down result against a criterion in this report first subtracts the offset of that output. Every range and every conclusion against a criterion is therefore stated at manufacturing scale.

The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its confidence interval. That conclusion is whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} n_fac` response-surface factors. Step yield and column efficiency have no criterion at the step. Their offsets are recorded, and no conclusion depends on them.

PCP-005 planned `{python} n_sd_plan` set-point runs of the scale-down model in the qualification study S-PA-SDM (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM')`), before the first run of the screening design. A further `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs were made in the supplementary qualification study S-PA-SDM2 (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM2')`) during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, to narrow the confidence interval of the offset for pool host cell protein. The plan did not foresee these runs, and they are recorded as the discrepancy from the plan PD-005-01 (@sec-dev). @tbl-sdm-offsets gives the offsets over all `{python} n_sd_all` scale-down runs, with `{python} off_df` degrees of freedom.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["protein_a"]).show()
```

For pool host cell protein the offset is `{python} f0(d_hcp)` ng/mg, with a confidence interval of `{python} f0(off_hcp['lo'])` to `{python} f0(off_hcp['hi'])` ng/mg that `{python} 'includes' if hcp_ci_zero else 'excludes'` zero. Subtracting the low end of the interval raises each prediction most, so the low end is the unfavourable end for an upper criterion.

Over the NOR as characterized, with protein load at `{python} load_nor_char` g/L resin, pool host cell protein `{python} 'meets' if nor_met_char_point else 'does not meet'` its criterion with the offset at its estimate. With the offset at the low end, the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run reaches `{python} f0(pl_char_lo)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, above the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. The conclusion therefore changes across the interval, and at the characterized NOR the model is not qualified for pool host cell protein. For this reason this report narrows the NOR of protein load to `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin. Over the narrowed NOR the same limit is `{python} f0(pl_new_lo)` ng/mg with the offset at the low end, and `{python} f0(pl_new_point)` ng/mg at its estimate. Pool host cell protein meets its criterion at both ends of the interval, and the model is qualified for it. The NOR of every other parameter is unchanged. Every result of this report judged against a criterion uses the narrowed NOR, and @tbl-sdm-offsets shows the qualification at it.

The offset was measured on the same laboratory columns as the designs. It therefore already contains any effect of the lower plate count of the laboratory column on how sharply the product elutes.

Leached Protein A is lower in the scale-down model. Its offset is `{python} f2(d_lpa)` ppm, and its confidence interval of `{python} f2(off_lpa['lo'])` to `{python} f2(off_lpa['hi'])` ppm lies wholly below zero. `{python} 'Each scale-down run was below the manufacturing mean.' if lpa_each_below else 'Most scale-down runs were below the manufacturing mean.'` The expected cause is the longer hold of the clarified harvest before capture at manufacturing scale. Protease activity in the clarified harvest is expected to rise while it is held. The load that reaches the column then carries more protease and cleaves more ligand from the resin during loading, and the cleaved ligand elutes with the antibody. This study does not test that cause. Each leached Protein A result of the designs is therefore raised by `{python} f2(abs(d_lpa))` ppm before it is compared with its criterion. The conclusion for leached Protein A is the same at both ends of the interval, and the model is qualified for it.

The offsets of the outputs without a criterion are `{python} f"{OFF.loc['step_yield', 'offset']:.1f}"` percentage points for step yield, `{python} f0(OFF.loc['plates_per_m', 'offset'])` plates per metre for column efficiency and `{python} f2(OFF.loc['asymmetry', 'offset'])` for peak asymmetry. They are recorded for PCMR-001, which summarises the offsets of the whole train.

Fragments by nrCE-SDS were not part of the qualification, because the method decision AMD-001 was taken after study S-PA-SDM had closed. Fragments therefore carry no offset (PCMP-001 §7.1). No adequate model results for fragments (@sec-rsm), so each fragment result is judged as measured. The scale-down model is taken as representative for fragments on mechanism. The capture of Fc-bearing species and low-pH hinge hydrolysis do not depend on scale at equal bed height, residence time and elution pH. The hold study measured attributes that the qualification did not compare, so its results also carry no offset.

## Operation

Each run followed SOP-2007 at laboratory scale. The column was equilibrated, loaded with clarified harvest to the target protein load, washed, and eluted with the elution buffer at the pH set by the design. The eluate was collected from the rise of the absorbance at 280 nm until the end of pool collect set by the design, in column volumes. The column was then stripped, cleaned and stored under SOP-2008. The pool was not neutralized, because the commercial eluate passes to low-pH viral inactivation at elution pH.

Each design was loaded from one pool of clarified harvest produced at set-point and held frozen in aliquots. A single feed keeps feed variation out of the estimated effects. The effect of feed quality on the step was therefore not estimated in these studies. The case study reports that Protein A capture is robust over a wide range of feed inputs [@amab2009], and the feed is characterized in PCR-003 and PCR-004. Runs were executed in random order within each design. The resin was used within the life-cycle limits of SOP-2008, and the life cycle of the resin is outside the scope of this report.

## Analytical methods

Each response was measured by a validated method under its own AMV. The controlled procedures and method validations used are listed below. The SOP and AMV numbers are placeholders.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=sops_pa, amvs=amvs_pa))
```

Pool host cell protein was measured by ELISA (AMV-3012) and is reported per mass of antibody in the pool, so that it does not depend on how far the pool is diluted by the end of pool collect. Step yield is the mass of antibody in the pool divided by the mass loaded, from the protein concentration by absorbance at 280 nm (AMV-3019) and the measured volumes. Leached Protein A was measured by ELISA (AMV-3016). Fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020, under SOP-3015), as PCMP-001 §7.8 sets for every step. SEC (AMV-3011) remains the method for aggregate, where no co-elution of this kind applies. Acidic variants in the hold study were measured by icIEF (AMV-3013), and residual DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014). @tbl-methods-by-study shows which method measured fragments in each design of the step, and Appendix D summarizes the methods.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study(["protein_a"]).show()
```

The screening design ran before the method decision AMD-001, and its pools were not retained. Its fragment results are by SEC only and are not used for any decision. The response-surface pools were retained frozen and were tested by nrCE-SDS in study S-PA-RET (`{python} win('S-PA-RET')`). On those pools SEC read fragments higher than nrCE-SDS by `{python} f2(sec_minus.min())` to `{python} f2(sec_minus.max())` percentage points (median `{python} f2(sec_minus.median())`). In this matrix part of the host cell protein elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC and is counted as fragment.

## Sampling plan

The load of each design was sampled once per feed aliquot thawed. The pool of every run was sampled once at the end of collection, after mixing, and its volume was recorded. Each pool sample was divided into aliquots for each method. One further aliquot of every response-surface pool was retained frozen under the sample management procedure of Analytical Development, and these are the samples tested by nrCE-SDS in study S-PA-RET. The screening design had `{python} cp_scr` centre points and the response-surface design `{python} cp_rsm`. Residual DNA was measured on the load and pool of the centre-point runs. The hold study was sampled as described in @sec-holddesign.

## Statistical methods

The designs were built and analysed under SOP-1002 with the common approach of PCMP-001 §6. Factors were coded from −1 to +1 over their range studied, with 0 at the centre. For each of the `{python} n_fac` design factors the centre of the range studied is the set-point, so the centre-point runs of both designs are set-point runs.

The screening data were fitted with a model of main effects and two-factor interactions. Effects are reported as the change in the response over the coded range of the factor, which is twice the coefficient. Significance was judged at α = 0.05. The screening model identifies effects. A two-level design cannot resolve curvature, so the screening model was not used to predict between its corners.

The response-surface data were fitted with a full quadratic model. This is the predictive model of the step, and every PAR and every prediction of a quality attribute in this report comes from it. Step yield is the exception, because its full quadratic model failed the limit on predictive power and was replaced by a reduced model (@sec-rsm). Coefficients are reported in coded units, so that each measures the change in the response over half the range studied. Effects quoted from them are twice the coefficient. Each model is reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R² (from PRESS), the model F-test, and the test of lack of fit against pure error from the centre points. A prediction of pool host cell protein or leached Protein A is translated to manufacturing scale by subtracting the offset of that output before it is compared with a criterion (@sec-sdm).

The adequacy criteria of PCP-005 §7 were applied as follows. The numbers are those of PCP-005 §7, where criterion 1 is the qualification of the scale-down model (@sec-sdm).

2. Model significance. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} g(lof_alpha)`.
3. Lack of fit. The lack of fit test is not significant at α = `{python} g(lof_alpha)`.
4. Predictive power. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f2(max_gap)`.
5. Residuals. Regressions of the absolute residuals on the predicted values, and of the residuals on run order, show no slope significant at α = `{python} g(lof_alpha)`, and no run has a Cook's distance above 4/n (`{python} f2(cook_lim)` for `{python} n_rsm` runs).

A model that fails criterion 3 or 4 was refitted with a justified change of terms, or it was not used to set a range. Where no adequate model resulted, the response is reported descriptively against its criterion over the runs of the design.

The PAR analysis follows PCMP-001 §6.4 and is described in @sec-par. Capability at commercial scale was estimated from the integrated model of the train, which runs `{python} mc_n` simulated batches with each parameter drawn within its NOR. Capability is reported as a one-sided Cpk against the drug substance criterion for each attribute of this step. It is judged against the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} f2(CPK_MIN)` that PCMP-001 §7.9 sets. The same simulation gives the probability that a drug substance batch falls outside its specification.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

@tbl-params lists the parameters of the step with their set-point, NOR, range studied, study type and the classification proposed in @sec-class.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(rp.reset_index(drop=True).assign(**{"Set-point": rp["Set-point"].map(g).values}), "Parameters of the Protein A step with set-point, NOR in force, range studied (Char. range), classification and study type.", "tbl-params",
        header={"Set-point": "Set-\npoint", "Char. range": "Char.\nrange"}, align=["P{3.4cm}", "P{1.4cm}", "r", "l", "l", "l", "l"],
        notes=[("", "The NOR of protein load is narrowed in this revision from " + load_nor_char + " g/L resin, the NOR the studies were run against, as the scale-down model section explains.")]).show()
```

Load flow rate is set as a linear velocity, so at the set-point bed height it fixes the residence time. The residence time is `{python} g(rt_set)` min at the set-point flow rate, and over the range studied it runs from `{python} g(rt_hi)` min at the highest flow to `{python} g(rt_lo)` min at the lowest. The upper end of the flow range therefore tests the shortest residence time against the highest load, which is the condition most likely to cause breakthrough. The lower end of the elution pH range tests the strongest elution and the largest release of weakly bound host cell protein. The upper end tests the weakest elution, with the broadest peak and the least co-eluting host cell protein. @tbl-legend gives the letter code of each design factor, which the coefficient tables and the appendices use. All `{python} n_fac` factors were studied in both the screening and the response-surface design.

```{python}

show(D.factor_legend_df(UO).drop(columns=["Studied in"]))
print()
print(": Letter codes of the design factors. {#tbl-legend}")
```

The execution window of every study of the step is recorded in @tbl-chronology. Each study began after PCP-005 Version 1.0 was approved on `{python} plan_appr`.

## Screening design

The screening design (study S-PA-SCR, `{python} win('S-PA-SCR')`) was a full two-level factorial design in the `{python} n_fac` factors, with `{python} n_fact` factorial runs and `{python} cp_scr` centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in all. Because the design is a full factorial, no effect is aliased with another, and every main effect and every two-factor interaction can be estimated. The responses were pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A, with fragments by SEC recorded for information. All `{python} n_fac` factors were carried into the response-surface design whatever the screening result, as PCP-005 §6.2 planned. The screening design therefore served to identify effects and interactions and to check the ranges. Appendix A gives the matrix and the results.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface design (study S-PA-RSM, `{python} win('S-PA-RSM')`) was a face-centred central composite design in the same `{python} n_fac` factors. It has `{python} n_fact` factorial runs, `{python} n_axial` axial runs at the faces of the cube and `{python} cp_rsm` centre points, `{python} n_rsm` runs in all. A face-centred design keeps every run inside the range studied. The full quadratic model leaves `{python} int(F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['model'].df_resid)` residual degrees of freedom, with `{python} F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['df_pe']` for pure error and `{python} F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['df_lof']` for lack of fit. The responses were pool host cell protein, step yield, leached Protein A and fragments by nrCE-SDS on the retained pools. Appendix B gives the matrix and the results.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-uni-design}

Operating temperature and bed height were studied one factor at a time in study S-PA-UNI (`{python} win('S-PA-UNI')`), with the other parameters at their set-points. Each was run `{python} uni_reps` times at the low and the high end of its range studied. The `{python} uni_n_ref` set-point runs of the planned qualification study S-PA-SDM served as the reference, as PCP-005 §6.4 planned. Bed height was varied at the set-point linear velocity, so that the residence time changed with it. The shortest bed gives a residence time of `{python} g(rt_short)` min, shorter than any run of the designs. The responses were pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A. Fragments were not measured in this study, which ran before the method decision AMD-001. The range of a univariate parameter is supported when every individual result at both ends meets its criterion at manufacturing scale, after the offset is subtracted (PCP-005 §6.4). A univariate study cannot detect an interaction. The ranges of these two parameters are therefore supported only with the other parameters at their set-points.

## Hold study of the Protein A eluate {#sec-holddesign}

The Protein A eluate is held at elution pH before viral inactivation. A pool produced at set-point was divided and held at `{python} t_cold` and `{python} t_warm` for up to `{python} h_days` days in study S-PA-HLD (`{python} win('S-PA-HLD')`). Samples were taken on days `{python} h_daylist` at each temperature. Aggregate and fragments were measured by SEC, and acidic variants by icIEF, at every sample point. The samples of days `{python} ce_days_txt` were retained and tested by nrCE-SDS in study S-PA-RET. Protein A capture does not separate aggregate or charge variants. The held eluate therefore carries the criteria that PCMP-001 sets for the output of the production bioreactor, ≤ `{python} agg_crit` % HMW and `{python} acid_crit` % acidic variants. Fragments are judged against the intermediate acceptance criterion of the pool, ≤ `{python} crit_frag` % by nrCE-SDS, on the days with an nrCE-SDS result.

The hold rule of PCP-005 §7 (criterion 7) limits the increase during the hold, not the level measured in the one held pool. The increase at a sample point is the result at that time minus the result on day 0 at the same temperature. A hold time is supported at a temperature when the largest increase up to that time, added to the highest level expected in the Protein A pool in manufacture, stays within the criterion. For aggregate and acidic variants the highest expected level is the upper 95 % prediction limit of the production bioreactor model within its NOR (PCR-003), because capture does not change them. No adequate model results for fragments at this step (@sec-rsm). For fragments the highest expected level is therefore the highest result measured on the retained pools of the response-surface design, which span the NOR and the range studied beyond it. The qualification of the scale-down model does not compare these attributes, so the hold results carry no offset.

# Results

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

The centre points of each design were run at set-point and estimate the pure error against which lack of fit is tested. @tbl-cp-rsm gives their mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation in the response-surface design, and @tbl-cp-scr in the screening design.

```{python}
#| output: asis
showt(tidy(D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm").replace({"Response": {L["step_yield"]: "Step yield (%)"}}), scale=["Mean", "SD"], scale_rows=["Step yield (%)"]))
print()
print(": Centre-point reproducibility in the response-surface design. {#tbl-cp-rsm}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
showt(tidy(D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening").replace({"Response": {L["step_yield"]: "Step yield (%)"}}), scale=["Mean", "SD"], scale_rows=["Step yield (%)"]))
print()
print(": Centre-point reproducibility in the screening design. {#tbl-cp-scr}")
```

Step yield was the most reproducible response, with a coefficient of variation of `{python} f2(cv_r.loc[L['step_yield'], '%CV'])` % in the response-surface design. Pool host cell protein reproduced to `{python} f2(cv_r.loc[L['pool_hcp_ng_mg'], '%CV'])` % in the response-surface design and to `{python} f2(cv_s.loc[L['pool_hcp_ng_mg'], '%CV'])` % in the screening design. The larger screening value makes the screening tests for pool host cell protein less sensitive than those of the response-surface design. Leached Protein A was the least precise response, at `{python} f2(cv_r.loc[L['leached_protein_a_ppm'], '%CV'])` % in the response-surface design. Its spread at the centre points is of the same size as its variation across the whole design. The variation of the ELISA and of the runs at set-point therefore masks any effect of the parameters of that size.

## Screening: factor effects

@tbl-scr-fit summarizes the screening models. The models for pool host cell protein and step yield are significant. The model for leached Protein A is not (`{python} pf(scr_fit.loc[L['leached_protein_a_ppm'], 'p-value'])`), and none of its terms is significant.

```{python}
#| output: asis
showt(tidy(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening").replace({"Response": {L["step_yield"]: "Step yield (%)"}}), scale=["RMSE"], scale_rows=["Step yield (%)"]))
print()
print(": Screening model summary (main effects and two-factor interactions). RMSE, root mean square error. {#tbl-scr-fit}")
```

Pool host cell protein was affected by elution buffer pH (B) and protein load (A), and by their interaction (AB). Raising the elution pH across its range lowered pool host cell protein by `{python} f0(abs(eH['B']['Effect']))` ng/mg, and raising protein load across its range raised it by `{python} f0(eH['A']['Effect'])` ng/mg. The interaction of protein load with elution buffer pH (`{python} f0(eH['AB']['Effect'])` ng/mg, `{python} pf(eH['AB']['p-value'])`) is negative, so the fall in host cell protein with rising pH is steeper at high load. Load flow rate and end of pool collect had no significant effect in the screening design. The effect of end of pool collect was positive in this design (`{python} f0(SV['D']['scr'])` ng/mg, `{python} pf(SV['D']['scr_p'])`), the opposite sign to the response-surface design (@sec-rsm). @tbl-scr-hcp gives the effects.

```{python}
#| output: asis
showt(tidy(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")))
print()
print(": Screening effects on pool HCP (ng/mg), sorted by size. {#tbl-scr-hcp}")
```

Step yield was affected by end of pool collect (D), protein load (A) and load flow rate (C), and by the interaction of protein load with load flow rate (AC). Extending the end of pool collect across its range raised yield by `{python} f"{100*eY['D']['Effect']:.1f}"` percentage points. Raising protein load and load flow rate lowered it by `{python} f"{100*abs(eY['A']['Effect']):.1f}"` and `{python} f"{100*abs(eY['C']['Effect']):.1f}"` percentage points. The interaction of protein load with load flow rate (`{python} f"{100*eY['AC']['Effect']:.1f}"` percentage points, `{python} pf(eY['AC']['p-value'])`) means that flow rate costs more yield at high load. The interactions of load flow rate with end of pool collect (CD) and of elution buffer pH with end of pool collect (BD) were also significant, at `{python} f"{100*eY['CD']['Effect']:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{100*eY['BD']['Effect']:.1f}"` percentage points. These are smaller than the main effects, and they were not confirmed in the response-surface design. Elution buffer pH had no significant effect on yield. @tbl-scr-yield gives the effects, and Appendix C gives the effects for leached Protein A.

```{python}
#| output: asis
showt(tidy(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "step_yield"), scale=["Effect", "Coef.", "Std. err."]))
print()
print(": Screening effects on step yield (percentage points), sorted by size. {#tbl-scr-yield}")
```

The screening results agree in direction with the expectations of @sec-prior. This holds for protein load, elution buffer pH and their interaction on pool host cell protein, and for every main effect and the interaction of protein load with load flow rate on step yield. A two-level design cannot attribute curvature to a factor, and the effects were refined in the response-surface design.

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

@tbl-adequacy judges each response-surface model against criteria 2 to 4 of PCP-005 §7. These are a significant model F-test, no significant lack of fit, and a predicted R² that falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f2(max_gap)`. Criterion 5, a Cook's distance below 4/n for every run with no trend in the residuals, is reported separately in @sec-resid.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(adeq_df, "Adequacy of the response-surface models against PCP-005 §7, criteria 2 to 4.", "tbl-adequacy",
        merge=["Response"], header={"R² − pred. R²": "Gap", "Lack of fit p": "LoF p",
                                    "Criteria 2–4 met": "Met", "Adj. R²": "Adj.\nR²", "Pred. R²": "Pred.\nR²", "Model p": "Model\np"},
        align=["P{2.8cm}", "P{1.9cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "c"],
        notes=[("", "Gap, R² minus predicted R² (limit " + f2(max_gap) + "). Model p, p-value of the model F-test. LoF p, p-value of the lack of fit test. "
                    "Met, criteria 2 to 4 of PCP-005 §7 all met (significant model, no lack of fit, gap within the limit). "
                    "The reduced model for step yield has the main effects of protein load, load flow rate and end of pool collect and their interaction AC, with an intercept.")]).show()
```

The model for pool host cell protein meets all three. The full quadratic model for step yield is significant and shows no lack of fit. Its predicted R², however, falls short of R² by `{python} f3(gap('step_yield'))`, more than the limit of `{python} f2(max_gap)`. It was therefore refitted with the terms that were significant in both designs, the main effects of protein load, load flow rate and end of pool collect and the interaction of protein load with load flow rate. The reduced model meets all three.
 The models for leached Protein A and fragments by nrCE-SDS are not significant (`{python} pf(F['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p'])` and `{python} pf(F['lmw_cesds_pct']['p'])`), and both have a negative predicted R². No adequate model results for them, and they are reported descriptively. `{python} "The same verdicts follow when predicted R² is compared with adjusted R², as PCMP-001 §7.2 states the criterion." if same_verdict_adj else "Compared with adjusted R², as PCMP-001 §7.2 states the criterion, the verdicts differ for at least one model."`

### Pool host cell protein

@tbl-coef-hcp gives the coefficients of the model for pool host cell protein, and @tbl-anova-hcp its analysis of variance.

```{python}
#| output: asis
showt(tidy(D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")))
print()
print(": Response-surface coefficients for pool HCP (ng/mg), coded units. {#tbl-coef-hcp}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
_an = D.anova_lof_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
showt(tidy(_an))
print()
print(": Analysis of variance with lack of fit for pool HCP (ng/mg). {#tbl-anova-hcp}")
```

The response-surface model confirms the screening result for protein load and elution buffer pH and refines it. Elution buffer pH (`{python} f0(cH['B']['Coef.'])` ng/mg per half range) and protein load (`{python} f0(cH['A']['Coef.'])` ng/mg) carry the largest coefficients. Their interaction is significant (`{python} f0(cH['AB']['Coef.'])` ng/mg, `{python} pf(cH['AB']['p-value'])`). At high load the pH coefficient is `{python} f0(slope_hi)` ng/mg per half range, and at low load it is `{python} f0(slope_lo)` ng/mg. The quadratic term in elution buffer pH is significant and positive (`{python} f0(cH['B²']['Coef.'])` ng/mg), so pool host cell protein rises more steeply at the low end of the pH range. The lack of fit test (`{python} pf(F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['p_lof'])`) is close to its limit.

End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein. Its coefficient is `{python} f0(cH['D']['Coef.'])` ng/mg per half range (`{python} pf(cH['D']['p-value'])`), an effect of `{python} f0(SV['D']['rsm'])` ng/mg across the range studied. Its interaction with protein load (AD, `{python} f0(cH['AD']['Coef.'])` ng/mg) makes the fall steeper at high load. Its interaction with elution buffer pH (BD, `{python} f0(cH['BD']['Coef.'])` ng/mg) makes the fall shallower at high pH. Collecting further into the tail of the elution peak adds antibody with little host cell protein, because the weakly held impurity elutes early, at the elution front. The host cell protein per mass of antibody therefore falls. It falls most where the early part of the peak carries most impurity, at high load and low pH.

The effect of end of pool collect and its two interactions reverse sign between the designs. In the screening design the effect of end of pool collect was `{python} f0(SV['D']['scr'])` ng/mg, and its interactions with protein load and elution buffer pH were `{python} f0(SV['AD']['scr'])` and `{python} f0(SV['BD']['scr'])` ng/mg. In the response-surface design they were `{python} f0(SV['D']['rsm'])`, `{python} f0(SV['AD']['rsm'])` and `{python} f0(SV['BD']['rsm'])` ng/mg. None of the screening estimates is significant, and each has a standard error of `{python} f0(scr_eff_se)` ng/mg. Noise alone does not explain the reversal, however. The screening results were compared with the predictions of the response-surface model at the same settings. Their difference depends on end of pool collect by `{python} f0(disc_D)` ng/mg across its range (`{python} pf(disc_D_p)`). Curvature does not explain it either. In a full factorial design the quadratic terms are confounded with the intercept, not with the main effect of end of pool collect. The cause was not identified (finding F11). The two designs were run at different times (@tbl-chronology), and a difference between their feeds or in how the end of collection was set could act in this way. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and the effect of end of pool collect is taken from it.

Load flow rate has no significant effect on pool host cell protein (`{python} pf(cH['C']['p-value'])`). Its interaction with protein load is not significant either (`{python} pf(cH['AC']['p-value'])`). Both point estimates are negative.

Across the response-surface design pool host cell protein ranged from `{python} f0(hcp_all_min)` to `{python} f0(hcp_all_max)` ng/mg in the scale-down model. At manufacturing scale, `{python} n_hcp_over` runs of the two designs exceeded the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, with results of `{python} f0(hcp_over_min_m)` to `{python} f0(hcp_over_max_m)` ng/mg. `{python} 'Each of these runs was at the highest protein load and the lowest elution buffer pH of the range studied, outside both NORs.' if hcp_over_corner else 'These runs lay at several settings of the design.'` @fig-contours shows the response surfaces of the scale-down model over protein load and elution buffer pH, with load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points.

```{python}
plt.show()
```

### Step yield

The reduced model for step yield has an intercept of `{python} f"{100*yred['Intercept']:.1f}"` %. Its coefficients per half range are `{python} f"{100*yred['coded_end_collect']:.1f}"` percentage points for end of pool collect, `{python} f"{100*yred['coded_load']:.1f}"` for protein load, `{python} f"{100*yred['coded_flow']:.1f}"` for load flow rate and `{python} f"{100*yred['coded_load:coded_flow']:.1f}"` for the interaction of protein load with load flow rate. At high load the coefficient of flow rate is `{python} f"{100*yC_hi:.1f}"` percentage points per half range. At low load it is `{python} f"{100*yC_lo:.1f}"`, so flow rate has almost no effect on yield when the bed has capacity to spare. Across the response-surface design step yield ranged from `{python} f"{y_min:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{y_max:.1f}"` %. Step yield has no acceptance criterion, and its model is used for the classification of parameters only. The coefficients of the full quadratic model are given in Appendix C.

```{python}
#| label: fig-diag-yield
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostics of the reduced response-surface model for step yield (protein load, load flow rate, end of pool collect, and the interaction of protein load with load flow rate)."
_fv = 100 * mY.fittedvalues.values; _rv = 100 * mY.resid.values; _sr = _rv / np.std(_rv, ddof=RED["k"])
_fig, _ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(11, 3.4))
_ax[0].scatter(_fv, _sr, s=18, color="#2a78d6"); _ax[0].axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.8)
_ax[0].set_xlabel("Predicted (%)"); _ax[0].set_ylabel("Std. residual"); _ax[0].set_title("Residuals vs predicted", fontsize=10)
sstat.probplot(_sr, plot=_ax[1]); _ax[1].set_title("Normal Q–Q", fontsize=10)
_act = 100 * dY["step_yield"].values; _lim = [min(_act.min(), _fv.min()), max(_act.max(), _fv.max())]
_ax[2].scatter(_act, _fv, s=18, color="#2a78d6"); _ax[2].plot(_lim, _lim, color="grey", lw=0.8)
_ax[2].set_xlabel("Actual (%)"); _ax[2].set_ylabel("Predicted (%)"); _ax[2].set_title("Actual vs predicted", fontsize=10)
_fig.suptitle("Model diagnostics, step yield (reduced model)", fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

### Leached Protein A

The leached Protein A model is not significant as a whole. One of its `{python} n_terms` terms, `{python} cL_sig[0]`, is significant, which is about what chance alone gives at α = 0.05. The centre points vary by `{python} f"{cv_r.loc[L['leached_protein_a_ppm'], '%CV']:.0f}"` %. A model this noisy cannot show that leached Protein A is independent of the parameters. It shows only that any dependence is too small to resolve against the variation of the runs. In the scale-down model leached Protein A ranged from `{python} f2(lpa_min)` to `{python} f2(lpa_max)` ppm across the runs of both designs. With the offset subtracted, the highest result corresponds to `{python} f2(lpa_max_m)` ppm at manufacturing scale. Against the intermediate acceptance criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm, every run `{python} 'met' if lpa_ok else 'did not meet'` the criterion (finding F5).

### Fragments by nrCE-SDS

Fragments by nrCE-SDS ranged from `{python} f2(fr_min)` to `{python} f2(fr_max)` % across the `{python} fr_n` retained pools of the response-surface design, against an intermediate acceptance criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %. The model as a whole is not significant. Within it, elution buffer pH has a significant negative coefficient (`{python} f3(cF.loc['B', 'Coef.'])` % per half range, `{python} pf(cF.loc['B', 'p-value'])`), so fragments fall slightly as elution pH rises. The size of the effect is small against the criterion. `{python} 'Every pool met the criterion.' if fr_ok else 'At least one pool did not meet the criterion.'` No PAR is claimed from the model (finding F6).

## Attributes measured for information

Aggregate by SEC was measured on every pool of both designs, for information. It ranged from `{python} f2(hmw_min)` to `{python} f2(hmw_max)` % HMW across the `{python} n_scr + n_rsm` pools, below the ≤ `{python} agg_crit` % that applies to the held eluate. This agrees with the expectation that Protein A capture does not separate aggregate from monomer, and that the short time at elution pH in the column forms little.

## Model residuals and influential runs {#sec-resid}

@tbl-resid gives the residual checks of criterion 5 of PCP-005 §7. The criterion asks for no trend of the residuals and a Cook's distance below 4/n for every run.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(res_df.rename(columns={"p, absolute residual\non predicted": "p, trend\n(predicted)", "p, residual\non run order": "p, trend\n(run order)",
                               "Largest Cook's\ndistance": "Max. D", "Runs\nabove 4/n": "D > 4/n"}),
        "Residual checks of the response-surface models (PCP-005 §7, criterion 5).", "tbl-resid", align="lrrrrr",
        notes=[("", "p, trend (predicted), p-value of the regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values. "
                    "p, trend (run order), p-value of the regression of the residuals on run order. "
                    "Max. D, largest Cook's distance, and the run that has it. D > 4/n, number of runs with a Cook's distance above 4/n (" + f2(cook_lim) + ").")]).show()
```

No model shows a slope of the absolute residuals on the predicted values (the smallest p is `{python} f3(min(RES[r]['p_slope'] for r in RESP))`). No model shows a slope of the residuals on the run order of execution either (the smallest p is `{python} f3(p_order_min)`), so no drift over the course of the design is seen. Every model, however, has runs above the Cook's distance limit of 4/n, between `{python} n_over_min` and `{python} n_over_max` per response. The limit on influential runs (criterion 5) is therefore not met for any response. A full quadratic model of `{python} int(F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['model'].df_model) + 1` terms in `{python} n_rsm` runs has a mean leverage of `{python} f2(mean_lev)`. The factorial and axial runs of a face-centred design carry high leverage by construction. Cook's distances above 4/n are therefore expected in this design, and the limit does not separate an influential run from a run at a corner.

For pool host cell protein, which is the only model used to set a range, each run above the limit was deleted in turn and the model refitted. The coefficients of protein load and elution buffer pH changed by at most `{python} f"{loo_dmax:.0f}"` %. Each refitted model was judged as the PAR analysis judges, on the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run over the NOR at manufacturing scale. That limit moved between `{python} f0(loo_lo)` and `{python} f0(loo_hi)` ng/mg, against `{python} f0(pl_new_point)` ng/mg for the full model. It `{python} "stayed below" if loo_ok else "did not stay below"` the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg in every case. No single run therefore decides the conclusion for pool host cell protein (finding F8). PCP-005 provides no alternative to the Cook's distance limit. Resting the conclusion on this influence analysis is work the plan did not provide for, and it is recorded as the discrepancy from the plan PD-005-02 (@sec-dev).

@tbl-hold-protein-a gives the results of the hold study.

The two temperatures started from aliquots of one pool. On day 0 these aliquots already differed by `{python} f2(h0['hmw_pct'])` % in aggregate, `{python} f"{h0['acidic_pct']:.1f}"` % in acidic variants and `{python} f2(h0['lmw_cesds_pct'])` % in fragments by nrCE-SDS (@tbl-hold-protein-a). This is the variation of the methods and of the aliquots, and a change smaller than it is not resolved.

At `{python} t_cold` the eluate changed little over `{python} h_days` days. Aggregate went from `{python} f2(hv(t_cold, 0, 'hmw_pct'))` to `{python} f2(hv(t_cold, h_days, 'hmw_pct'))` % and acidic variants from `{python} f"{hv(t_cold, 0, 'acidic_pct'):.1f}"` to `{python} f"{hv(t_cold, h_days, 'acidic_pct'):.1f}"` %. At `{python} t_warm` aggregate and acidic variants rose more. Aggregate went from `{python} f2(hv(t_warm, 0, 'hmw_pct'))` to `{python} f2(hv(t_warm, h_days, 'hmw_pct'))` % and acidic variants from `{python} f"{hv(t_warm, 0, 'acidic_pct'):.1f}"` to `{python} f"{hv(t_warm, h_days, 'acidic_pct'):.1f}"` %. Aggregate rose by `{python} f2(hd[(t_warm, 'hmw_pct')])` % at `{python} t_warm` against `{python} f2(hd[(t_cold, 'hmw_pct')])` % at `{python} t_cold`.
