Fragments by nrCE-SDS rose from `{python} f2(hv(t_cold, 0, 'lmw_cesds_pct'))` to `{python} f2(hv(t_cold, h_days, 'lmw_cesds_pct'))` % at `{python} t_cold` and from `{python} f2(hv(t_warm, 0, 'lmw_cesds_pct'))` to `{python} f2(hv(t_warm, h_days, 'lmw_cesds_pct'))` % at `{python} t_warm`, rises of `{python} f2(hd[(t_cold, 'lmw_cesds_pct')])` and `{python} f2(hd[(t_warm, 'lmw_cesds_pct')])` %. The difference between these rises, `{python} f3(frag_gap)` %, is `{python} frag_gap_word` the difference of `{python} f3(h0['lmw_cesds_pct'])` % between the day 0 aliquots. The data therefore do not show that fragmentation in the held eluate depends on temperature.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mech}

Pool host cell protein rises as elution buffer pH falls. A lower pH protonates more histidine and acidic residues, which disrupts the electrostatic association of host cell protein with the antibody and with the resin, so more host cell protein is released with the product. The positive quadratic term in pH shows that this release accelerates at the low end of the pH range. Pool host cell protein also rises with protein load, as in the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. Host cell protein that travels with the antibody rises in proportion to the antibody and cannot raise the value per mg. This study does not establish the mechanism of the load effect. The two parameters interact, and the fall of pool host cell protein with rising pH is steeper at high load.

End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein per mass of antibody in the response-surface design. Collecting further into the tail adds antibody and little host cell protein, so the ratio falls. The same extension raises yield, which is the largest single effect on yield in both designs. The mechanism does not explain why the effect of end of pool collect on pool host cell protein had the opposite sign in the screening design (finding F11).

A higher load flow rate shortens the residence time and lowers the dynamic binding capacity. This costs yield only when the bed is close to capacity, which is why the cost appears at high load and nearly vanishes at low load. Load flow rate has no significant effect on pool host cell protein.

Leached Protein A could not be modelled, and the mechanism gives no reason for it to follow the settings of a single run. The expected cause of the offset of leached Protein A between the two scales, the protease activity of the held load, is not a setting of a run (@sec-sdm).
 Fragments by nrCE-SDS fall slightly as elution pH rises, which is the direction expected from acid-catalysed hinge hydrolysis during elution. The effect is small because the antibody spends only the duration of the elution at low pH in the column.

For operation, elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and the risk lies in the corner of low pH and high load. End of pool collect is also associated with pool host cell protein. Within its NOR it moves the boundary of that corner little (@sec-ds). Load flow rate is associated with lower yield at high load.

# Design space {#sec-ds}

The design space of this step is the region in protein load and elution buffer pH, the two WC-CPPs, over which pool host cell protein meets its intermediate acceptance criterion at manufacturing scale. Leached Protein A and fragments met their criteria in every run of the designs, and step yield has no criterion, so they do not constrain it. On the mean predictions of the response-surface model, with load flow rate and end of pool collect at their set-points, `{python} f"{ds2_sp:.1f}"` % of the region of protein load and elution buffer pH studied meets the criterion. The excluded region is the corner of high protein load and low elution buffer pH. It lies wholly below the elution buffer pH NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])`, at pH `{python} f"{ds_ph_max:.2f}"` and below, and it reaches down to a protein load of `{python} g(round(ds_load_min, 1))` g/L resin, `{python} 'inside' if ds_in_load_nor else 'above'` the protein load NOR of `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin. At that corner the model predicts `{python} f0(corner_m)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, against ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. At the corner of the two NORs it predicts `{python} f0(nor_corner_m)` ng/mg. With load flow rate and end of pool collect at the corners of their NORs, the fraction of that region lies between `{python} f"{ds2_min:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{ds2_max:.1f}"` %. With load flow rate at its set-point and end of pool collect at the low and the high edge of its NOR, the fraction is `{python} f"{ds2_dlo:.1f}"` % and `{python} f"{ds2_dhi:.1f}"` %. Over the whole range studied of all `{python} n_fac` factors, `{python} f"{ds_frac:.1f}"` % of the design region meets the criterion.

A region defined on mean predictions is not a claim for a single batch. At the boundary of such a region a single batch meets the criterion only about half the time [@amab2009]. The claim is therefore made through the PARs of @sec-par, which use the 95 % prediction interval of a single run.

Over the NOR the model predicts a mean pool host cell protein between `{python} cr_hcp_range` ng/mg at manufacturing scale (@tbl-criteria-protein-a). The upper limit of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run reaches at most `{python} f0(hcp_nor_pi_max)` ng/mg over the NOR, `{python} 'below' if hcp_nor_pi_ok else 'above'` the criterion. Movement outside the NOR and within a PAR would be assessed under change control.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

## Acceptance basis

Each output of the step is judged against the intermediate acceptance criterion that PCMP-001 §7.3 derives a priori, as PCP-005 §8.1 applies it. The drug substance criterion is carried backward through the train using the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform with X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and no margin is applied. PCMP-001 §7.5 then lets the A-Mab data of a downstream step replace a platform worst case, in either direction. @tbl-iac-verification gives the downstream values on which the criteria of this step rely.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.worst_case_verification(["viral_inactivation", "cex", "aex"]).show()
```

The rows that matter here are host cell protein at cation exchange and anion exchange, fragments at low-pH viral inactivation and cation exchange, and leached Protein A at cation exchange and anion exchange. The other rows serve the criteria of other steps.

For pool host cell protein the drug substance limit of ≤ `{python} ds_hcp` ng/mg is carried back through cation exchange and anion exchange. With the platform worst cases of `{python} g(v_cex_hcp['assumed'])`-fold and `{python} g(v_aex_hcp['assumed'])`-fold clearance, the a priori criterion was ≤ `{python} apri_hcp` ng/mg. The criterion in force is ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg, with the basis "`{python} basis_hcp`". It was widened by the rule of PCMP-001 §7.5. Under that rule the A-Mab value replaces a platform worst case only where two conditions hold. The one-sided 95 % confidence bound of the A-Mab worst case within the NOR must be better than the platform value. The response-surface model of the downstream step must also pass the adequacy tests of PCMP-001 §7.2, on lack of fit and on how far predicted R² falls short of R². The point prediction is never used. PCMP-001 stated this rule before any Version 2.0 report applied it.

The widened value rests on cation exchange alone. The cation exchange model, from `{python} n_rsm_cex` runs with `{python} cp_rsm_cex` centre points, predicts a lowest host cell protein clearance within its NOR of `{python} f2(v_cex_hcp['predicted_nor'])`-fold. This value is the lowest over every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the response-surface factors of cation exchange. Its one-sided 95 % confidence bound, `{python} f2(v_cex_hcp['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold, carries the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients and is better than the platform value of `{python} g(v_cex_hcp['assumed'])`-fold. The model passes both adequacy tests. Predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f2(v_cex_hcp['r2_minus_pred_r2'])`, within the limit of `{python} f2(max_gap)`, and the lack of fit test gives p = `{python} f"{v_cex_hcp['p_lack_of_fit']:.2f}"`. The bound therefore replaced the platform value.

The anion exchange model, from `{python} n_rsm_aex` runs with `{python} cp_rsm_aex` centre points, gives a bound of `{python} f2(v_aex_hcp['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold, also better than its platform value of `{python} g(v_aex_hcp['assumed'])`-fold. It is not credited, because its predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f2(v_aex_hcp['r2_minus_pred_r2'])`, more than the limit of `{python} f2(max_gap)`. A model that predicts left-out runs this much worse than it fits its own runs cannot carry a criterion upstream. The platform value stands for anion exchange. The cation exchange bound and the anion exchange platform value give a clearance of `{python} fold_hcp`-fold and a criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg.

The widened criterion holds only while cation exchange runs within its NOR. At the edges of its range studied, the lowest host cell protein clearance measured in a cation exchange run was `{python} f2(v_cex_hcp['observed_edge'])`-fold, below the platform value. The models of the two steps are reported in PCR-007 and PCR-008.

For fragments the drug substance limit of ≤ `{python} ds_frag` % is carried back through cation exchange and then through the largest increase of low-pH viral inactivation. The criterion in force is the a priori value, ≤ `{python} crit_frag` %, with the basis "`{python} basis_frag`". Both downstream bounds are better than their platform values. They are `{python} f2(v_cex_frag['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold for the fragment clearance of cation exchange, against `{python} f2(v_cex_frag['assumed'])`-fold, and `{python} f2(v_vi_frag['predicted_nor_bound95'])` percentage points for the fragment increase of low-pH viral inactivation, against `{python} g(v_vi_frag['assumed'])`. Neither is credited, because both fragment models fail the predictive power test. Predicted R² falls short of R² by `{python} f2(v_cex_frag['r2_minus_pred_r2'])` for cation exchange and by `{python} f2(v_vi_frag['r2_minus_pred_r2'])` for low-pH viral inactivation. The platform values of `{python} fold_frag`-fold and `{python} add_frag` percentage points therefore stand.

For leached Protein A the drug substance limit of ≤ `{python} ds_lpa` ppm is carried back through cation exchange and anion exchange, which together remove it `{python} fold_lpa`-fold on the platform. That gives ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm, with the basis "`{python} basis_lpa`". Leached Protein A is not a response of the cation exchange or anion exchange designs, so the platform values for its clearance cannot be checked in this campaign, and they stand. `{python} "Every other downstream value on which these criteria rely was confirmed or bettered by its A-Mab data." if rel_all_conf and rel_unchk_lpa else "Not every downstream value on which these criteria rely was confirmed."` No criterion of this step was tightened. No criterion upstream of this step relies on a worst case of the Protein A step, so this report carries no verification of its own.

For a quality attribute the value compared with the criterion is the limit of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run, because a single batch is what must meet a quality criterion (PCMP-001 §6.4). In the NOR-propagated analysis the model coefficients are drawn from their estimated covariance in every simulated run, together with the residual. The prediction of pool host cell protein or leached Protein A is translated to manufacturing scale by subtracting its offset before it is compared with the criterion.

# Parameter classification {#sec-class}

Parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. The classification rule of PCP-005 §7 (criterion 8) adds that an effect is practically relevant for an attribute when the NOR-propagated PAR of the parameter is narrower than its range studied. It also states that a significant effect whose PAR spans the whole range studied does not by itself make the parameter critical. At this step that one-factor test identifies elution buffer pH, whose PAR for pool host cell protein is narrower than its range studied. The PAR of protein load spans its range studied, but its effect is relevant all the same. Together with elution buffer pH it takes pool host cell protein above its criterion within the range studied, in the corner of high load and low pH (@sec-ds). Its NOR is also narrowed by this report, because the qualification of the scale-down model for pool host cell protein depends on it (@sec-sdm). The classes and the reason for each are the following.

- Protein load was classified as a WC-CPP. It raises pool host cell protein (`{python} f0(cH['A']['Coef.'])` ng/mg per half range) and interacts with elution buffer pH, and with it bounds the design space. It is set by the load volume and the titre, and it is readily controlled within its NOR. The NOR is narrowed in this revision from `{python} load_nor_char` to `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin, so that the scale-down model is qualified for pool host cell protein over it (@sec-sdm). Its PAR spans the range studied of `{python} rng(P['load'])` g/L resin.
- Elution buffer pH was classified as a WC-CPP. It has the largest effect on pool host cell protein (`{python} f0(cH['B']['Coef.'])` ng/mg per half range), and with protein load it bounds the design space. Buffer pH is controlled at preparation and verified at release. Its PAR for pool host cell protein, `{python} hcp_par_nor['elution_ph']`, is narrower than its range studied of `{python} rng(P['elution_ph'])` and wide against its NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])`. The deviation DEV-005-01, an elution buffer prepared below its target pH, shows that a buffer below the NOR can pass release when the pH meter is incorrectly calibrated.
- Load flow rate was classified as a KPP. It lowers step yield at high load. A faster load shortens the residence time, which lowers the dynamic binding capacity, and near saturation of the bed this lets antibody break through. It has no significant effect on pool host cell protein, leached Protein A or fragments.
- End of pool collect was classified as a KPP. It has the largest effect on step yield. It also has a significant effect on pool host cell protein, `{python} f0(SV['D']['rsm'])` ng/mg across the range studied, and the sign of that effect differs between the designs (finding F11). Its NOR-propagated PAR for pool host cell protein spans the whole range studied. Across its NOR, the share of the region of protein load and elution buffer pH studied that meets the criterion moves from `{python} f"{ds2_dlo:.1f}"` % at the low edge to `{python} f"{ds2_dhi:.1f}"` % at the high edge (@sec-ds). The class would be revisited if a later study confirmed the screening sign.
- Operating temperature was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['temperature'])` ng/mg. Such a rise `{python} 'would still leave pool host cell protein within its criterion at manufacturing scale' if uni_ub_ok['temperature'] else 'could take pool host cell protein above its criterion'`, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni).
- Bed height was classified as a GPP. No difference from the set-point runs was detected at either end of its range. The intervals allow a rise in pool host cell protein of up to `{python} f0(uni_ub['bed_height'])` ng/mg, and every individual result met its criterion (@sec-uni). Bed height is fixed by the packing specification of the commercial column and does not vary in operation. A short bed at the upper end of the load range was not characterized, and no claim is made for it.

In summary the step has `{python} n_wc` WC-CPPs, `{python} n_kpp` KPPs and `{python} n_gpp` GPPs, and `{python} "no CPP" if n_cpp == 0 else f"{n_cpp} CPP"`. The classes of protein load and elution buffer pH rest on the size of their effects, on the PAR of elution buffer pH, and on the corner where the two parameters take pool host cell protein above its criterion together. Both effects agree in direction with the A-Mab case study. The KPP classes rest on the reduced model for step yield, on the direction of the yield effects in both designs, and on the mechanism of breakthrough and of peak collection.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-cs}

The Protein A step contributes to the control strategy in the following ways.

1. Process parameters. Protein load and elution buffer pH are controlled within their NORs as WC-CPPs. The NOR of protein load is `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin, narrowed from `{python} load_nor_char` g/L resin in this revision (@sec-sdm). Load flow rate and end of pool collect are controlled within their NORs as KPPs. Movement outside the NOR and within the PARs of @sec-par is assessed under change control.
2. Material controls. Elution buffer is released against its pH specification. The elution buffer prepared below its target pH (DEV-005-01) showed that this release test depends on a correctly calibrated pH meter.
3. Resin and load. Leached Protein A depends on the life of the resin and on the protease activity of the load. Resin use, cleaning and sanitization are controlled by SOP-2008. The hold of the clarified harvest before capture, the expected cause of the offset of leached Protein A between the scales (@sec-sdm), is characterized in PCR-004.
4. Hold. The Protein A eluate may be held at elution pH for up to `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm` before viral inactivation.
5. Downstream clearance and release. Host cell protein, leached Protein A and fragments are further cleared by cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008), and they are tested at release of the drug substance. The criterion for pool host cell protein relies on cation exchange running within its NOR (@sec-par). Viral clearance is claimed at low-pH viral inactivation (PCR-006), anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-009), and not at this step.

The control strategy of the whole train is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The characterization confirms the main effects expected for this step. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and they interact. The mechanism of the load effect is not established, because pool host cell protein is reported per mg of antibody. End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. One result does not follow the expectations. End of pool collect lowers pool host cell protein in the response-surface design and raised it, not significantly, in the screening design, for a reason that was not identified.

The scale-down model is qualified by its offset for both outputs with a criterion, but for pool host cell protein only after two changes. At the protein load NOR as characterized, the conclusion for pool host cell protein changed across the confidence interval of the offset, so the NOR was narrowed to `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin. On the `{python} n_sd_plan` planned runs the interval was too wide for a qualification even at the narrowed NOR, and `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs were added (PD-005-01). Both changes were made after the Version 2.0 re-analysis had shown the result on the planned runs. The rule and the criterion were not changed. The narrowing costs routine operation the upper `{python} g(LOAD.nor_characterized[1] - LOAD.nor[1])` g/L resin of the load NOR. Leached Protein A is lower in the laboratory column, for the expected cause given in @sec-sdm. Subtracting its offset raises each result by `{python} f2(abs(d_lpa))` ppm, and the highest result of the designs stays far below its criterion at `{python} f2(lpa_max_m)` ppm. The supplementary runs narrowed the confidence interval of the offset for pool host cell protein by `{python} f"{narrow_pct:.0f}"` % (@sec-dev). The offset was estimated at set-point only. The report therefore assumes that it is the same across the ranges studied, and this assumption is not tested.

The criterion for pool host cell protein now depends on the cation exchange bound of `{python} f2(v_cex_hcp['predicted_nor_bound95'])`-fold. Within its NOR cation exchange clears host cell protein better than the platform worst case, at the one-sided 95 % confidence bound, and its model passes the adequacy tests. At the edges of its range studied it cleared less than the platform value. The criterion of this step therefore holds only while cation exchange runs within its NOR. Anion exchange is credited with its platform value only, because its model fails the predictive power test.

The response-surface model for pool host cell protein is significant, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on predictive power, with a lack of fit test close to its limit. It does not meet the limit on influential runs, a Cook's distance below 4/n, and no model does. The conclusions on pool host cell protein rest instead on the deletion of single runs, which showed that no run decides them. The Cook's distance limit of 4/n is better suited to a design with low leverage than to a face-centred design with `{python} int(F['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['model'].df_model) + 1` terms in `{python} n_rsm` runs. A limit based on the leverage of each run would serve the purpose of the criterion better. The residuals show no trend with the run order of execution (@tbl-resid).

Leached Protein A and fragments gave no adequate model. For both, any effect of the parameters is small against the variation of the runs and the assay.

The `{python} n_dev` deviations of the study did not change its conclusions (@sec-dev). The elution buffer prepared below its target pH (DEV-005-01) was below the NOR but inside the range studied. The out-of-trend leached Protein A result (DEV-005-02) was replaced by a valid re-assay.

The other limitations are those the plan named. Each design used one feed, so the effect of feed quality on the step was not estimated. The limits of the univariate study are stated in @sec-uni-design. The laboratory column does not reproduce the hold of the manufacturing load before capture, and the offset of leached Protein A is expected to carry that difference.

# Conclusions

1. The step was characterized under PCP-005 in a screening design, a response-surface design, a univariate study and a hold study.
2. The scale-down model is qualified by its offset for leached Protein A, and for pool host cell protein at the narrowed protein load NOR of `{python} load_nor_new` g/L resin, on all `{python} n_sd_all` set-point runs. At the NOR as characterized, `{python} load_nor_char` g/L resin, it is not qualified for pool host cell protein. Leached Protein A is lower in the scale-down model, and every judgement subtracts its offset.
3. Elution buffer pH and protein load have the largest effects on pool host cell protein, and it falls as the end of pool collect is extended. Its model is significant, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on predictive power. Because no model met the limit on influential runs, its conclusions rest on an influence analysis. End of pool collect, protein load and load flow rate have the largest effects on step yield. Leached Protein A and fragments met their criteria in every run, and no adequate model results for either.
4. Every output met its intermediate acceptance criterion across the NOR in force at manufacturing scale. The NOR-propagated PAR for pool host cell protein is `{python} hcp_par_nor['elution_ph']` for elution buffer pH and spans the range studied for the other parameters. Pool host cell protein exceeds its criterion only at high protein load with elution buffer pH below its NOR.
5. Protein load and elution buffer pH are WC-CPPs, load flow rate and end of pool collect are KPPs, and operating temperature and bed height are GPPs. The step has no CPP.
6. No difference from the set-point runs was detected for operating temperature or bed height, and their ranges studied are supported with the other parameters at their set-points.
7. The eluate may be held at elution pH for `{python} h_days` days at `{python} t_cold` or `{python} t_warm`.
8. At commercial scale the lowest Cpk among the attributes of this step is `{python} f2(cpk_hcp)`, for host cell protein, against the target of `{python} f2(CPK_TARGET)` set in PCMP-001.
9. The `{python} n_dev` deviations were investigated and the data retained without changing the conclusions. The supplementary set-point runs and the influence analysis are recorded as discrepancies from the plan. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

The full quadratic model for step yield was replaced by a reduced model (PCP-005 §7, @sec-rsm), and leached Protein A and fragments were reported descriptively (PCP-005 §5.5). No run was lost or invalidated, and no design was repaired or re-executed.


## DEV-005-01. Elution buffer pH below target on a response-surface run

The elution buffer of lot LOT-BUF-5290 was prepared below its target pH. It was used on run `{python} dev_run` of the response-surface design, whose design setting for elution buffer pH was `{python} g(dev_ph_design)`. The buffer had passed release on an incorrectly calibrated pH meter. The error was found at a review of the buffer preparation record after the run, and the pH of the lot was `{python} g(dev_005_01_ph_measured)`. This is below the NOR of `{python} nor(P['elution_ph'])` and inside the range studied of `{python} rng(P['elution_ph'])`. The investigation found an error at the titration end point during buffer preparation.

The run gave a pool host cell protein of `{python} f0(dev_hcp_obs)` ng/mg at manufacturing scale, `{python} 'below' if dev_obs_ok else 'above'` the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. At the recorded pH of the buffer lot the model predicts `{python} f0(dev_hcp_pred_meas)` ng/mg, and the result is `{python} 'well below' if dev_below_meas else 'above'` that prediction. At the design setting the model predicts `{python} f0(dev_hcp_pred_design)` ng/mg, and the result is `{python} 'closer to it' if dev_closer_design else 'further from it'`. The result does not show the rise in pool host cell protein that a buffer at the recorded pH would be expected to cause. The data do not establish why. The run was analysed at its design setting. There its residual is `{python} f0(dev_resid)` ng/mg, `{python} 'within' if dev_resid_small else 'larger than'` one residual standard deviation of the model (`{python} f0(fH['rmse'])` ng/mg). Its Cook's distance for pool host cell protein is `{python} f2(dev_cook)`, `{python} "above" if dev_cook_over else "below"` the limit of 4/n. `{python} "Deletion of the run, as for every run above the limit, does not change the conclusion for pool host cell protein" if dev_cook_over else "The run does not influence the fit more than the other runs of the design"` (@sec-resid). The run was retained. The release test is the control on which the WC-CPP class of elution buffer pH relies, and here it did not detect the error because the meter was incorrectly calibrated. Run `{python} dev_run` carries a footnote in Appendix B.

## DEV-005-02. Leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` initially out of trend

The leached Protein A result of run `{python} dev_005_02_run` of the response-surface design was out of trend at analytical review. The sample was re-assayed under AMV-3016. The investigation attributed the first result to suspected carryover in the ELISA. The re-assay result, `{python} f2(dev02_val)` ppm in the scale-down model, is the one reported in Appendix B and used in the analysis. The first result was kept in the record with its status marked. The re-assay result lies `{python} 'inside' if dev02_in_range else 'outside'` the range of the other runs of the design. At manufacturing scale it is `{python} f2(dev02_val - d_lpa)` ppm, `{python} 'far below' if dev02_ok else 'above'` the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_lpa` ppm.

## PD-005-01. Supplementary set-point runs in the scale-down model qualification

PCP-005 planned `{python} n_sd_plan` set-point runs of the scale-down model in the qualification study S-PA-SDM, compared with `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches. During the Version 2.0 re-analysis, while INV-001 was open, a further `{python} n_sd_supp` set-point runs were made in study S-PA-SDM2 (`{python} win('S-PA-SDM2')`). They were made to narrow the confidence interval of the offset for pool host cell protein, which is the output that sets the ranges of the step. The plan did not foresee these runs. They were made under the same procedures as the planned runs.

With all `{python} n_sd_all` runs the half-width of the interval for pool host cell protein is `{python} f0(off_hcp['half'])` ng/mg, against `{python} f0(off_hcp0['half'])` ng/mg on the planned runs alone, `{python} f"{narrow_pct:.0f}"` % narrower. @tbl-sdm-offsets-planned gives the qualification on the `{python} n_sd_plan` planned runs alone.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets(["protein_a"], studies=["S-PA-SDM"], label="tbl-sdm-offsets-planned").show()
```

On the planned runs the offset for pool host cell protein is `{python} f0(off_hcp0['offset'])` ng/mg (`{python} f0(off_hcp0['lo'])` to `{python} f0(off_hcp0['hi'])` ng/mg), and for leached Protein A `{python} f2(off_lpa0['offset'])` ppm (`{python} f2(off_lpa0['lo'])` to `{python} f2(off_lpa0['hi'])` ppm). On the planned runs alone the model would not be qualified for pool host cell protein, even at the narrowed protein load NOR. With the offset at the low end of the wider interval, the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run over that NOR reaches `{python} f0(pl_plan_lo)` ng/mg, above the criterion of ≤ `{python} crit_hcp` ng/mg. For leached Protein A the model is qualified on the planned runs alone. On all `{python} n_sd_all` runs it is qualified for both outputs (@tbl-sdm-offsets).

The supplementary runs therefore changed the qualification for pool host cell protein. The decision to make them was taken after the result on the `{python} n_sd_plan` planned runs was known. The qualification rule of PCMP-001 §7.1, the criterion and the confidence level were not changed, and every run that was made is used.

## PD-005-02. Pool host cell protein conclusion resting on an influence analysis

PCP-005 planned to set the ranges and the design space from a response-surface model that meets every model adequacy criterion of PCP-005 §7. No model of the step met the limit on influential runs (criterion 5), a Cook's distance below 4/n for every run (@sec-resid). The model for pool host cell protein is significant, shows no lack of fit and meets the limit on predictive power. Its conclusions rest on an influence analysis that the plan does not describe, in which each run above the limit was deleted in turn and the model refitted. With any one of these runs deleted, the upper 95 % prediction limit of a single run over the NOR at manufacturing scale stays `{python} "below" if loo_ok else "above"` the criterion.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.doe_results("protein_a", "rsm").show()
```

## Appendix D. Analytical methods summary {.unnumbered}

@tbl-methods-summary summarizes the analytical methods used in the studies of the step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_md_rows = [
    ("ELISA", "Host cell protein", "AMV-3012", "ng per mg antibody", "Response of both designs, univariate study"),
    ("ELISA", "Leached Protein A", "AMV-3016", "ppm", "Response of both designs, univariate study"),
    ("UV absorbance at 280 nm", "Protein concentration", "AMV-3019", "step yield, %", "Response of both designs, univariate study"),
    ("Non-reduced CE-SDS", "Fragments (LMW)", "AMV-3020", "% of total", "Response of the response-surface design, hold study"),
    ("SEC-HPLC", "Fragments (LMW)", "AMV-3011", "% of total", "Information only"),
    ("SEC-HPLC", "Aggregate (HMW)", "AMV-3011", "% of total", "Hold study, information"),
    ("icIEF", "Acidic variants", "AMV-3013", "% of total", "Hold study"),
    ("qPCR", "Residual DNA", "AMV-3014", "pg per mg antibody", "Information only"),
]
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_md_rows, columns=["Technique", "Analyte", "AMV", "Reportable", "Use in this report"]),
        "Analytical methods used in the studies of the Protein A step.", "tbl-methods-summary",
        merge=["Technique"], align=["P{2.4cm}", "P{2.8cm}", "l", "P{2.2cm}", "P{4.4cm}"]).show()
```
